analysis:
Reviewed the supplied batch analysis against the replayed patches and canonical definition index, including the detailed T-041 contract. In provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Engine/Bridge/EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift, HEAD lines 15, 32 and 64 add and forward an optional CBv2StopStringScope; lines 150–151 pass it into terminal matched-stop reporting. The visible changes do not modify emitted response chunks, encryption, authorization, token accounting, cancellation or cache cleanup. No concrete security regression is established by this evidence.

The libs/mlx-swift-lm pin at HEAD line 1 changes executable dependency behavior, but the dependency implementation diff is unavailable. Integration still needs to verify scoped stop matching, reasoning/tool channel transitions, prompt-opened reasoning, native block exceptions, and consistency between engine termination and terminal metadata. Request-scope construction at runPump callers and EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift replay behavior are also unverified. These contracts matter to consumer-controlled inference behavior, availability and output integrity (A-001, A-018, TB-007, T-007, T-010); the dependency must also preserve resource retirement and cache isolation assumptions (T-028, T-041).

Replay is explicitly incomplete: three reviewed source units, including documentation and surrounding BASE source described by the prior analysis, are omitted. Thus its claims about documentation and retained cleanup paths cannot be independently confirmed here. No visible change establishes a new attestation, billing, credential, installer or plaintext-exposure issue. Further review of the changed dependency and scope-plumbing implementations is required before reaching a security conclusion about the combined stop-handling change; missing evidence is not itself a finding.
